title: Shared canonicalization conformance vectors (WS-CANON-UNIFY Phase 0)
notes: One vector set run by uvrn-core (canonicalSerialize), uvrn-receipt (canonicalize), and uvrn-identity (canonicalize, local copy).

JSON cannot express undefined / NaN / Infinity / array holes, so inputs use $uvrn hydrate tokens: { "$uvrn": "undefined" | "NaN" | "Infinity" | "-Infinity" | "sparseHole" }. Test-side hydrate() replaces tokens with the real value; sparseHole becomes a true array hole (delete arr[i]).
expect is the strict RFC 8785 (JCS) outcome: { "canonical": string } or { "error": true }.

knownDivergence pins CURRENT behavior per implementation (Phase 0 characterization — pinned, not skipped, not fixed). A package with a knownDivergence entry asserts that pinned behavior instead of expect. Removing a pin requires a Phase B behavior change with its own golden-hash regression proof (ADR-006, ADR-010).

Decision-1 evidence (2026-07-16, run against compiled dist of all three packages): true sparse [1,<hole>,2] emits '[1,,2]' (invalid JSON) in ALL THREE implementations — Array.prototype.map preserves holes and join renders them empty — so sparse-hole is a SHARED pin. Dense [1,undefined,2] emits '[1,,2]' in core only; receipt/identity emit '[1,null,2]' — core-only pin.
Do not edit SPEC/vectors/canonical.json for divergence cases; that file is the frozen receipt-v1 contract.

vectors.description: Recursive sorting through nested objects and arrays
Non-ASCII keys/values pass through JSON.stringify escaping; control chars escaped
ECMAScript number serialization: -0 → 0, 1e21 boundary, small exponent
Top-level string with quote, backslash, newline, backspace escapes
Empty array, empty object, empty string
undefined-valued property: strict impls omit the member; core emits malformed JSON

core.note: Malformed JSON — dangling member value. Evidence 2026-07-16.

vectors.description: Dense array containing undefined: strict impls emit null; core drops the value between commas

TRUE sparse array (hole, not undefined value). Decision-1 evidence: ALL THREE emit identical invalid JSON '[1,,2]' because Array.prototype.map preserves holes and join renders them empty — shared pin, not core-only

receipt.note: Shared divergence: map((item) => item === undefined ? 'null' : ...) never visits holes. Evidence 2026-07-16.

identity.note: Shared divergence: byte-identical local copy of receipt serializer. Evidence 2026-07-16.

vectors.description: Top-level NaN: strict impls throw; core silently emits null

core.note: Silent NaN → null via JSON.stringify. Evidence 2026-07-16.

vectors.description: NaN inside an array: strict impls throw; core emits [null]
NaN-valued property: strict impls throw; core emits null member value
Infinity: strict impls throw; core silently emits null
-Infinity: strict impls throw; core silently emits null
Top-level undefined: strict impls throw; core returns the empty string

core.note: Empty string — hashes to sha256 of zero bytes. Evidence 2026-07-16.
